Elliott Prechter: Teaching a Machine to Count Elliott Waves | Market Cycles Report August 6, 2026
🌎 FREE Cycles Newsletter: https://cycles.org/free-newsletter/

Elliott waves have always depended on the analyst counting them. Elliott Prechter spent the past decade teaching a machine to do it instead. In this episode of the FSC interview series, *Elliott Prechter* explains how R.N. Elliott's fractal five-three structure from the 1930s becomes software: scale-invariant pattern recognition, an *elliotticity* score that grades every wave count from 0 to 100 percent, and published research showing the model can distinguish real market data from randomized data.

Elliott Prechter speaks with Lars von Thienen, board member of the Foundation for the Study of Cycles, about wave patterns versus time cycles, why a form-based market model stays stable when quantitative models break, and what automation changes for wave analysis in practice.

Elliott Prechter is President of Qualitative Analytics, developer of the EWAVES symbolic AI engine, and son of Robert Prechter.
